info.name: HunarHub API — Full Backend Suite
info.description:
All 31 endpoints across the 6 route modules in server/routes/, generated directly from the source (routes, models, middleware) rather than guessed from the outside. Companion to the Resume Defense Audit — every request's description ties back to something specific in the code, including the two gaps that audit flagged (the isApproved product-creation gap, and the unfinished category-matching endpoint).

Setup: run `npm run seed` in server/ first (needed for the Login — Seeded Admin request), then `npm run dev` from the repo root, then run folders top-to-bottom once. Re-running Auth twice will 409/400 on the unique email fields — register with fresh emails or clear the collection variables.

item.name: 0 · Health
item.description: One request, no auth: proves the process is alive before anything else runs.

request.description: Not behind /api in the router sense — mounted directly in server.js. Confirms the server process and CORS/JSON middleware are wired before touching anything stateful.

item.name: 1 · Auth
item.description: 3 routes in routes/auth.js: register, login, me. Run top-to-bottom once per environment — registration will 400 on a repeat run since email is unique.

request.description: Baseline registration. Captures buyerToken/buyerId for every buyer-scoped request below.
This account starts with isApproved:false in the database — see the 'Approve Entrepreneur' request in the Admin folder. Captures sellerToken/sellerId.

Regression test for the mass-assignment fix in routes/auth.js: SELF_SERVICE_ROLES = ['buyer','seller']. Sends role:'admin' and asserts the server refuses to honor it. This is the executable proof behind the resume-defense audit's Bullet 2 caveat.

exec: pm.test('role is silently downgraded to buyer, NOT admin', () => pm.expect(data.role).to.eql('buyer'));

request.description: Requires `npm run seed` to have been run first — uses the demo admin account seed.js creates. Captures adminToken for the whole Admin folder.
Verifies the protect middleware: token in, current user out. The password-absence assertion is the direct proof of Phase 4/Bullet 3's select:false + .select('-password') claim.

exec: pm.test('No password field — select: false is working', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.not.have.property('password'));

item.name: 2 · Admin
item.description: 9 routes in routes/admin.js, every one protect + authorize('admin'). Runs right after Auth so its Create Category output is available to later folders.

request.description: User.find({ role:'seller', isApproved:false }) — should include the seller registered above.

Flips the boolean. Per the audit: this changes visibility in the public entrepreneur directory (Categories folder below) — it does NOT retroactively affect the seller's existing ability to list products, which was never gated in the first place.

Backed by Order.aggregate([{ $group: { _id:null, total:{ $sum:'$totalPrice' } } }]) for totalRevenue — a real aggregation pipeline, not a JS sum. Numbers will be low/zero if run before the Orders/Service Requests folders.
Unlike the public GET /categories, this does not filter by isActive.
Captures categoryId, used by the Categories and Service Requests folders below.
findByIdAndUpdate with runValidators:true — a bad enum/type here should 400, not silently coerce.
Cross-user overview — populates customer, entrepreneur, and category. Re-run this after the Service Requests folder to see non-empty results.
Isolated from categoryId above on purpose — deleting the shared category would break the Service Requests folder.
Deletes only the throwaway category created above.

Run this on its own, not as part of a full top-to-bottom collection run — it flips the same seller back to unapproved, which would break the 'Entrepreneurs for Category' request in the Categories folder if it runs afterward.

item.name: 3 · Categories
item.description: 3 public routes in routes/categories.js — no auth header on any of these.

request.description: Public — no Authorization header sent.

Known gap from the Phase 4 audit: this ignores categoryId and returns every approved seller, not sellers matched to that category — the route comment admits it. Only returns results once 'Approve Entrepreneur' has run.
Public profile lookup — works regardless of approval status.

item.name: 4 · Products
item.description: 6 routes in routes/products.js — the fullest CRUD surface in the API, plus the nested review sub-resource.

request.description: Exercises the dynamic query-builder: category $in, price $gte/$lte, sort. Try adding &search=pottery to hit the $regex/$or branch too.
multipart/form-data — Multer's upload.array('images', 5) runs before this handler. Requires authorize('seller'); notably does NOT check isApproved (see the audit).

formdata.value: Wheel-thrown terracotta vase, fired in a traditional kiln.

formdata.description: Optional — select up to 5 image files to test the Multer upload path. Works fine with none too.

request.description: Also runs a second query for Review.find({product}) and merges it into the response as `reviews`.
Ownership-checked: product.seller.toString() === req.user._id.toString(). Try running this with {{buyerToken}} instead to see the 403.

Also triggers the aggregate-rating recompute on the Product document. Run this request a second time and expect 400 'You already reviewed this product' — that's the compound index's application-level backstop.
Isolated from productId above — deleting the shared product would break the Orders and Add Review requests.
Deletes only the throwaway product created above.
seller is copied from the product document server-side — the client never supplies it directly.
Order.find({ buyer: req.user._id }) — a buyer can only ever see their own orders, there's no orderId lookup-by-id route at all.
authorize('seller') gate — try this with {{buyerToken}} to see the 403.
Ownership-checked against order.seller — ownership here, not just role.
Only checks entrepreneur.role === 'seller' — does not require isApproved, matching the audit's Bullet 2 finding.

request.description: authorize('seller') gate.
Ownership-checked against request.entrepreneur.

Run in isolation. There is no status-machine guard in this route — calling reject after complete above will silently overwrite status back to 'rejected'. Worth knowing that's how it behaves if asked about state validation.
